answers.answer: For four players, select 3 randomly chosen Escape Pod tokens. Place the lowest-numbered in Section A, next in numerical order in B, then alternate A/B; all start Locked side up. The bag starts with 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults, plus 1 additional Adult per player (so 7 Adults for four players).
answers.evidence: Setup step 7: ‘3 pods for 3–4 players’ and ‘All pods start with their Locked side face up’; step 10 gives the starting token mix.

answers.answer: Remove Objective cards showing a player count higher than the actual player count from both Corporate and Personal decks, shuffle separately, then deal each player 1 of each. At the First Encounter (first Intruder miniature appearing), each player chooses 1 of their 2 and removes the other face down without looking. Eggs do not trigger this choice because they are not Intruders.
answers.evidence: Setup step 16; Special Rules: ‘First Encounter’ and ‘Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this.’

answers.answer: Discard the played Action card plus two additional Action cards to pay its printed cost of 2; the two Contamination cards cannot pay. If it offers OR effects, choose one section/effect.
answers.evidence: Actions: ‘discard that card face up and pay its cost by discarding the required number of additional Action cards’; Contamination cards ‘can never be discarded to pay any Action cost’; ‘OR’ means choose one.

answers.answer: They take 1 Light Wound after finishing their own round, including the round in which they pass. After passing they cannot take further Actions this Player Phase, but when passing they may discard any number of cards. Later players’ rounds do not cause additional Fire damage to them; damage is only after their own round, once that turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘ends their round in a Room with a Fire marker suffers 1 Light Wound’; ‘only after finishing their own round’; passing players take it once at the end of their round and no more that turn.

answers.answer: On entering an unexplored Room, flip the tile face up and reveal its Exploration token. Set the Item count by rotating the tile so its number faces the board’s Item Counter (except Nest/Room Covered in Slime), then resolve and remove the token. Noise is rolled only if the Room is empty. Silence suppresses the movement Noise roll (unless Slime converts it to Danger); Danger suppresses it and draws eligible neighboring Intruders into the Room, or places Noise in all connected empty corridors if none are eligible. An already occupied destination means no Noise roll. The summary does not explicitly state the destination for a Noise roll that hits a corridor already marked; elsewhere it specifies an Encounter for a second marker.
answers.evidence: Movement: flip unexplored tile/reveal token; Noise roll if empty, not if anyone is there. Exploration tokens and Noise roll detail effects; ‘A Corridor may never hold more than 1 Noise marker… resolve an Encounter instead.’

answers.answer: Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards and replaces the usual Noise roll after moving with placing a Noise marker in a chosen connected Corridor of the destination. It is forbidden in Combat and if all destination-connected Corridors already have Noise. Closed Doors block Character movement between Rooms; miniatures can never stop in Corridors. The summary does not explicitly say Careful Movement can cross a Closed Door, though the general rule says a Closed Door blocks ‘neighboring’ status for players’ Movement.
answers.evidence: Basic Actions: Careful Movement costs 2, substitutes a marker for Noise, and lists restrictions. Movement: ‘no one may ever stop in a Corridor’; ‘A Closed Door blocks the “neighboring” status for players’ Movement.’

answers.answer: The rolled number points to a corridor that already has Noise, so resolve an Encounter. First discard all Noise markers from all corridors connected to the Room (including Technical Corridors if it has an Entrance); draw one token, place its matching miniature unless it is Blank, then compare token number with the triggering player’s hand size counting Action and Contamination cards. Fewer cards than the number causes a Surprise Attack against that triggering Character. Contamination cards count for this comparison, even though they cannot pay Action costs.
answers.evidence: Noise roll: placing on an occupied corridor resolves an Encounter. Encounter sequence explicitly says discard connected Noise, draw/place token, and compare against triggering player’s Action AND Contamination cards.

answers.answer: Danger moves all neighboring Intruders that are not in Combat with any Character into the destination. If none are eligible (none nearby or all are in Combat), place Noise markers in every connected Corridor that lacks one, counting Technical Corridors if there is an Entrance. An Intruder moving into a Character’s Room is not an Encounter. Slime changes Silence to Danger.
answers.evidence: Exploration token ‘Danger’: ‘move ALL eligible Intruders’; otherwise noise in each connected corridor. Encounter section: an Intruder merely moving into a Room with a Character is NOT an Encounter. Slime section: every Silence becomes Danger.

answers.answer: In an Encounter, Blank places a Noise marker in each Corridor connected to the Room, returns to the bag, and no miniature appears. If it was the last token in the bag, add 1 Adult token if available. In bag development, Blank adds 1 Adult token if available and is returned to the bag; the summary does not give additional Noise placement for bag development.
answers.evidence: ‘Blank token in an Encounter’ specifies noise, last-token condition, and return. Event Phase bag development: ‘Blank — add 1 Adult Intruder token to the bag… Return the Blank token to the bag.’

answers.answer: Both Intruders stay in their starting Room and destroy the Closed Door; the summary says they destroy it simultaneously and all stay put. A Destroyed Door can never be Closed again (except via Plasma Torch). A Noise-triggered appearance through a Closed Door is not blocked; the Intruder appears regardless.
answers.evidence: Door tokens: ‘several Intruders moving from the same Room destroy it simultaneously and all stay put’; Destroyed ‘can never be Closed again’; Noise appearance ‘regardless of the Door.’

answers.answer: An Intruder entering a Technical Corridors Entrance disappears: remove its miniature, discard all Injury markers, and return its token to the bag. A Noise marker on the Technical Corridors space remains. Characters normally cannot use Technical Corridors (exceptions are named character/item abilities), and Door tokens can never be placed there.
answers.evidence: Technical Corridors: Intruder ‘discard all its Injury markers, return its token to the Intruder bag, and remove its miniature’; Noise marker is not removed; Characters can never use them; Doors never placed there.

answers.answer: Both Shoot and Melee cost 1 Action card and target one Intruder in your Room. Shoot requires a Weapon in Hand with ammo, discards 1 Ammo, then rolls the Combat die; it does not add Contamination. Melee draws 1 Contamination card into the Action discard pile, then rolls; a miss also causes the Character 1 Serious Wound. In Melee, a two-hit result counts as one Injury (and the 2-Injury result is reduced to 1).
answers.evidence: Combat section: Shoot cost/weapon/ammo/target; Melee cost/draw Contamination/miss consequence; two-hit melee reduction.

answers.answer: After damage, Larva (and Egg) dies at 1 Injury. Adult: draw 1 Intruder Attack card and compare its blood value to current injuries; it dies if blood is equal to or lower than injuries. Queen: draw 2 cards, add blood values, compare in the same way. A dead Adult or Queen leaves an Intruder Carcass in its Room (Carcasses for any dead Intruder except Larvae; the summary’s direct list also includes Creepers). If any Queen check card shows Retreat, it flees: draw an Event card and move it through the Corridor number in its movement section, then discard that Event card.
answers.evidence: Intruder Injuries and death lists Larva/Egg at 1, Adult 1 card and Queen 2 cards added; Carcass except Larvae. Retreat: Queen/Breeders retreat if either drawn card shows Retreat.

answers.answer: Before moving, resolve one Intruder Attack per Intruder in the current Room. Escape attacks target the escaping Character. If they die, their Corpse remains in the Room they tried to leave. If they survive, complete movement to the neighboring unexplored Room, reveal its tile/token, then because the destination is empty make a Noise roll (unless the revealed Exploration effect such as Silence or Danger modifies/suppresses it).
answers.evidence: Character Escape: before moving, one attack per Intruder; survive completes move and Noise/exploration; if die Corpse stays in the Room tried to Escape from. Movement/exploration rules give reveal and empty-room Noise.

answers.answer: With several Characters, the Intruder targets the player with the fewest Action cards in hand; ties go to the First Player token holder (or next player in turn order). Draw one Intruder Attack card; matching Intruder symbol means hit and resolve effect, otherwise miss. A Larva does not draw an Attack card: remove it from the board and place it on the target’s Character board, and that target gains 1 Contamination card, placed on top of their Action discard pile.
answers.evidence: Intruder Attack targeting/tie and symbol match rules; Infest (Larva attack) and Contamination card placement sections.

answers.answer: A Character with 3 Serious Wounds dies instantly upon suffering any additional Wound, including a Light Wound; dressing a wound suppresses its effect but it still counts toward the limit. A third Light Wound clears the Light Wound track and causes a Serious Wound. Heal removes a Light Wound or discards a Dressed Serious Wound card as specified. On death, place a Character Corpse token in the Room and drop all Heavy Objects there.
answers.evidence: Character Wounds: 3 Serious Wounds plus any additional Wound kills; Dressed Serious Wound still counts; third Light converts; Heal; death and dropped Heavy Objects.

answers.answer: Canteen and Shower scan only Contamination cards in the player’s HAND, removing all non-Infected ones; infected results place a Larva (if one is already on the board, the Character dies and a Creeper appears). Surgery scans all Contamination cards in deck, hand, and discard, removes all Infected ones, and removes a Larva if present. Surgery also causes 1 Light Wound, automatically passes the player, and shuffles all Action cards (including hand) into their deck. The summary does not state whether Surgery removes non-Infected Contamination cards.
answers.evidence: Room Actions: Canteen/Shower scan all hand Contamination and remove non-Infected; Surgery scans deck/hand/discard and removes all Infected, Larva handling, Light Wound, automatic pass, shuffle.

answers.answer: For uncarried Eggs in the Room, Shoot or Melee attempts deal Injuries and each Injury destroys one Egg. A missed Melee causes neither Contamination nor a Wound. Grenades destroy 2 Eggs, Molotov destroys 1. Roll Noise after every single attempt to destroy an Egg. Fire destroys 1 uncarried Egg during each Fire Damage step. When no Eggs remain in the Nest (carried away or destroyed), the Nest is destroyed and marked with 1 Injury. The summary does not say a specific Noise-roll exception for grenade/Molotov attempts; it says after every attempt.
answers.evidence: Eggs and the Nest: attack, waived penalties, grenade/Molotov quantities, Noise after each attempt, Fire destruction, and Nest destruction.

answers.answer: To enter, use the Evacuation Section A/B Room Action for an Unlocked Pod with room in that Section. Make a Noise roll first; if an Intruder appears or is present in the Room, entry fails; Escape Pod rules also say you cannot enter if the Room has an Intruder or Malfunction. A Pod holds up to 2 Characters; Heavy Objects take no Character space. You may launch immediately or wait. While waiting, you can launch at the start of your first round in each Player Phase or exit for free; if you do not launch in your round, you automatically pass. If an Intruder appears in the Evacuation Room while waiting, all Pod occupants return to that Room. Another Character entering the Pod may launch it immediately. The summary does not give a separate explicit consequence for a failed entry beyond failure to board.
answers.evidence: Escape Pods: unlocked/manual/automatic; entry through Section Room Action and Noise roll; two Characters per Pod; Heavy Objects no space; waiting options and consequences.

answers.answer: Victory checks run: Engines, Coordinates, Contamination, then Objectives. If 2 or 3 Engines are Damaged, the ship explodes and all hibernating Characters die. If destination is not Earth, all hibernating Characters die, except a Quarantine Objective holder survives hibernation if destination is Mars. Survivors (hibernating or evacuated) undergo Contamination checks: scan all Contamination in deck, discard pile, and hand; if any is Infected, shuffle all cards and draw 4, dying if any Contamination is among them. A Character with a Larva skips scanning and does the draw-four check directly. Pod passengers are included in the Contamination check.
answers.evidence: Victory Check enumerates all four steps and specifically says each surviving Character (hibernating or evacuated) checks Contamination; Engine and Coordinates conditions included.
